content.body:
Upgunned and uparmoured, the newest revision to the now-venerable PzKw.III series granted it new life. The armor upgrades make some of the armor (front and rear) now effective against the common British 2pdr. ATG. The Kwk.50L42 50mm gun boasted a big increase in hitting power over the earlier 37mm gun but still struggled against the heavier British and French tanks of the period. It achieved fame in the desert battles of North Africa, as the Pz.IIIh could finally fight toe-to-toe against British medium tanks. By mid war, this tank was made instantly obsolescent by the surprise of the Russian T34 with which it neither could trade shots nor be upgunned further to do so better.
Control variations: none, identical to the PzIIIf.
Recognizable by its extended turret bustle, the Pz.IIIh is seductive. As the first well-armored German turreted tank in the field, its possible to be lulled into too much of a sense of security by the AP rounds bouncing off your now thicker mantlet. The 50mm gun is much more lethal, combined with the characteristically superior German sights this means that the Pz.IIIh is extremely effective, especially compared with its ancestors. Despite this, the 50mm gun remains unable to penetrate the fronts of the Char.B1 and the Matilda, and the thicker armour you get upgraded with is only on the front hull/turret and the rear hull. Your flanks are still vulnerable particularly to side turret hits.
This tank is quite good at overwatch duty for smaller, less capable tanks. Be their "big brother" and lend extra effectiveness to them with your greater combat ability. Alternatively, sit at the rear of a wedge or reversed-wedge formation in company with heavier tanks like StuG's and Pz.IVg's, and screen the flanks of your formation while the "heavies" engage in the frontal aspect. Continue to play the tank carefully, recognizing the danger particularly of flank or rear shots. Your commander is only useful if hes able to see ... leave him unbuttoned almost all the time (pull him in during air attack or if you are entering an urban area) ... if he is killed, the slight risk to your tank (through his open hatch which will then remain open) will have been more than offset by his utility to that point if you have used him to spot for you.
Move quickly from cover to cover, use shadows and brush to break up your outline as much as possible.
